title: Dorothy Arnold
subtitle: New York, 1910
voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.
grade: Desaturated documentary still, New York City in December 1910, grey winter light and light snow, melancholy and uncanny, period 1910 detail, cinematic composition, fine film grain. Single image, not a collage, one continuous scene, no split frame, no text, no signage, no people, no faces.

beats.vo: On December twelfth, nineteen ten, Dorothy Arnold, twenty-five, left her family's home in Manhattan to go shopping.
beats.img: The front steps and door of an elegant Upper East Side brownstone on a grey December morning in 1910, light snow on the railings, empty street.

beats.vo: She charged a box of chocolates. She bought a book, at Brentano's, on Fifth Avenue.
beats.img: A wrapped 1910-style box of chocolates and a small cloth-bound book with a plain blank cover resting on a shop counter, soft winter window light.

beats.vo: Just before two o'clock, she ran into a friend, and said she would walk home through Central Park.
beats.img: A single winding footpath through Central Park in winter 1910, bare trees, an old iron lamppost and an empty wooden bench, light snow, no buildings in frame, no street, no people.
Interior of an elegant 1910 Manhattan dining room at evening, a dinner table set with china, one empty chair, warm gaslight, heavy curtains drawn, still and quiet, no people.

beats.vo: Sightings, letters, and confessions all came to nothing. No trace of her has ever been confirmed.
beats.img: Fifth Avenue at dusk in winter 1910, empty snowy sidewalk, gas street lamps glowing, a few distant carriages, melancholy.

facts.claim: Vanished December 12, 1910, age 25; left home ~11 a.m. to shop (for a dress); family lived in Manhattan (Upper East Side)
Charged a half-pound box of chocolates (Park & Tilford); bought a book at Brentano's (Fifth Avenue & 27th St)
Met friend Gladys King shortly before 2 p.m.; said she would walk home through Central Park
Never returned home; sightings, a postcard, ransom notes, a 1916 prisoner's burial claim all unverified/false; no confirmed trace; fate unknown
